Kamelhalsfliege.et:
Kamel (“camel”) + Hals (“neck”) + Fliege (“fly”). Compare Slovene kamelovratnica (< kamela + vrat).

Kamelie.et: It was named after Moravian Jesuit missionary, pharmacist and naturalist Joseph Kamel (‘Camellus’) (1661–1706). The Czech surname Kamel is a variant of Kamil, who gave a description of the plants of East Asia.

Kampf.et: From Middle High German kampf, from Old High German kampf, from Proto-West Germanic *kamp (“field, battlefield”). The word originally referred to the “battlefield”, but early on developed the sense “battle, fight” in High German.

Kamm.et: From Middle High German kamb, camb, chamb, from Old High German chamb, from Proto-West Germanic *kamb, from Proto-Germanic *kambaz, from Proto-Indo-European *ǵómbʰos (“tooth”).
